If you are thinking of making more humans, there are alot of things you should know to emotionally prepare yourself as much as possible. Some things it seems like no one ever talks about but we need to know these things for own own well being as potential parents and for the long term well being of our offspring.

  1. You may not bond with your baby right away because new born babies are terribly uninteresting people. You are not a terrible person. For some people the shock and awe of having made such a completely helpless human can get through the first months of potato time. For others, you won't feel engaged until baby starts to show glimmers of their personality 3 months in. Men bond through actions, so encourage fathers to play with baby.

  2. Even the newest of babies have feelings. Don't believe psychologist and their bench marks. Babies don't know what is going on but they do have feelings and you will greatly cut down crying time if you recognize that and adjust your behavior accordingly. For instance: babies see poorly and they have no concept of going and returning so when you disappear from their limited line of sight they panic and cry.

  3. Babies have different cries for different things https://youtu.be/_IRQc2hOiKE

  4. It is not normal for babies to be always gasey, constipated and constantly spit up huge amounts of milk. This is what happens when you feed a baby formula. A breastfed baby will have much more stable and predictable digestion, be more sated, less prone to illness and generally happier. When you use formula, it also accumulates residue over time in the babies mouth especially the tongue causing even more problems. Nowadays, if we have problems getting babby to latch to the breast we can buy pumps and bottle feed.

  5. Babies like to be carried and you are not spoiling them in anyway by carrying them as much as possible. They can hear your heart beat, they are comforted by the sway of your walking and they can see you. Invest in a comfortable and safe baby carrier and go about your day normally. In my experience, if they get their fill of being carried early, they tend to be less clingy later.

  6. Encourage babies to move around and use their bodies and build strength. Even little babies have a desire to play and interact with you but they can't move around too well. Simple things like waving your arms around and opening and closing your hands can be very fun and exciting for a new human and they will try to mimic you. You should move their arms and legs for them until they can do it themselves.

  7. Babies stare but hardly blink. Most of the time, your new potato will we asleep but they have moments of lucidity where they wake up and try to take in the world. Try to give them something interesting to look at.

  8. Small things have to be fed frequently, including in the middle of the night. You can't avoid this. Most baby mammals will need to be feed every 3-4 hours. In my grandmother's time, women slept with their babies and would just let the baby suckle while the mother slept some people now feel this practice is unsafe. Babies do know how to root around for a nipple

  9. There are times when you will get overwhelmed and you may feel like you want to shake or injure your baby. This is just truth of life; it happens. Sometimes your baby will become unconsolable and you might have to endure hours of crying and it may become too much for you. Put the baby down, eat something, get hydrated, call someone to help with baby for a bit while you recharge. Take turns holding and comforting baby.

  10. Babies have different personalities. Some babies are shy and clingy, some are bold and independent, others are grumpy and impatient. Sometimes you get lucky and you get a baby with a mellow temperament but be prepared to deal with different personalities and cater your care accordingly.

 

Need practice? Go borrow a baby. People love free baby sitters. You can sometimes just volunteer to watch while the parents do chores and what not.
